name: Bariis iskukaris
subtitle: Bariis iskukaris is a traditional one-pot rice dish from Somalia.

parts.text: Bariis iskukaris is a traditional one-pot rice dish from Somalia. It is made with basmati rice and seasoned with xawaash, a Somali spice blend, with warm spices such as cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cardamom and clove; raisins are often added.
In Somali homes and restaurants rice is served with a banana, which is sliced into the rice rather than eaten separately, and it is eaten with meats such as goat or chicken.

blocks.title: Bariis iskukaris (1-pot Somali rice & chicken)
blocks.sub: One version of the dish, as given by NHS (Healthier Families); the steps are summarised in our own words. Recipes differ from cook to cook.
blocks.note: A lower-calorie version published by the NHS; the steaming time is given as 10 to 15 minutes.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pan and soften the onion and garlic over medium heat.
Stir in the cinnamon, cumin seeds and tomatoes and cook over medium heat, stirring often.
Add the chicken, the ground spices, the crumbled stock cube and the carrot; mix and cook over medium-high heat, stirring now and then.
Pour in 400 ml of the water, cover and simmer over medium heat until the chicken is almost cooked.
Stir in the rice so it is coated, add the remaining 200 ml cold water, cover and bring to a bubble over medium-high heat.
Lower the heat and let the rice steam, covered, until tender and fluffy.
Serve, with fresh coriander on top if wanted and a green salad alongside.
